public_rationale: This is a forecast with no deadline that whatever users pay for AI services will change. Since the post, there have been some changes. Google stopped selling Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise plans on October 9, and it has announced a doubling of a Gemini API price from December 1. But an index built from official price pages found no list-price changes among 17 models and plans from September to October 2026. Typical subscriptions stayed at $20 and top plans at $200. Scattered changes do not show that prices across the board are changing, and two months of stable prices do not disprove an open-ended forecast. So it stays unresolved.
limitations: Some evidence is secondary summaries of official pages.
The claim's universal 'whatever you're paying' and lack of a deadline make it hard to settle.
Changes in usage per price (like Anthropic's limit cut) could count under a looser reading.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Because AI companies have not worked out their business models, current AI service pricing will change.

statement.excerpt: And the fact they haven’t worked out their business models means that whatever you’re paying today is guaranteed to change.

from_speaker: the fact they haven’t worked out their business models
our_interpretation: Plain reading: the price people pay today for AI services (subscriptions and API) will change, because vendors have not settled their business models.
The context also treats lower value at the same price as a change. I note that reading but take the plain reading to be about what is paid, meaning price or plan terms.
No deadline is stated. Because the claim covers 'whatever you're paying', one vendor's change does not settle it. Settling it requires broad changes across the major services.
criteria.support_condition: After the post, the major AI services (for example ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor) change their prices or the plans users pay for, with the changes tied to business-model or cost pressure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Over a long period, the main AI service prices and plan terms stay the same.

evidence.excerpt: A typical AI subscription cost $20.00 a month (no change), and top plans cost $200.00 (no change).
evidence.explanation: Two months after the post, median subscription prices had not changed and median API prices had fallen. That is consistent with an open forecast but shows no broad repricing yet.

evidence.excerpt: Gemini 4 Argon (Google) from December 1, 2026: input $2.00 → $4.00, output $10.00 → $20.00 per million tokens.
evidence.explanation: An announced doubling of a Google API price shows some prices users pay today will change. But it takes effect after the evaluation date and ends an introductory price.

evidence.excerpt: Since 9 October 2026, you can't buy new Standard or Enterprise subscriptions.
evidence.locator: section 'Product changes that matter more than price'
evidence.explanation: A paid AI product was withdrawn from sale after the post, a change in what users can pay for. It is one product, not a broad price change.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Price or plan-term changes for the main paid plans of several leading AI services after August 2026, documented on official pricing pages. Or, against it, those prices holding over a long period such as a year or more.
